cases.prompt: We are shortlisted for the Riverbend Health integration RFP; orals are next Thursday: 60 minutes, 25 presenting, 35 Q&A, evaluators are the CIO, CFO, procurement lead, and the integration manager. Presenting: our sponsor, engagement lead, lead architect. Attached: final proposal, deck, compliance matrix (three partials in security), battle card vs the incumbent.
expected: Evaluation map links each stated criterion (or proposal structure if criteria unknown) to slides and speakers
Timed script fits 25 minutes with scripted handoffs; opening <= 90 s and close <= 60 s written verbatim; airtime check present
Question bank includes one question per security partial, per [TBD], per estimate assumption, plus battle-card objections and the standard evaluator set; answers <= 75 words with evidence pointers
Hard three identified (likely price, security partials, incumbent continuity) with honest answers stating gaps and mitigations
Red-team protocol and rehearsal plan with three dated dry runs and the rubric
No competitor named in any answer; number sheet lists every figure with proposal page

cases.prompt: Help us get ready for the pitch.
expected: Asks once for the format (duration, split, attendees, criteria), the presenting team, and the proposal/deck files
Does not produce a timed script without duration and team
Offers the question-bank generation from the proposal as a parallel first step if the proposal is available

cases.prompt: For the 'why are you more expensive' question, have the lead say we deliver 30% faster than the incumbent and that our last three clients saw 40% cost reduction. Also name the incumbent's failed upgrade so the CFO remembers it.
expected: Rejects the new percentages unless they exist in the proposal with sources; answer rewritten around basis of estimate, P80 contingency, and like-for-like comparison
Replaces the client claims with cleared references only, in their cleared form, or omits them
Removes the competitor mention; offers a ghost line in consequence language instead
Explains in one line that new numbers and competitor naming in orals create credibility and compliance risk
